question: A team lead on a Team plan wants a shared project whose instructions the whole team relies on. Which sequence of steps is correct?
options: A) Save them as project instructions; share the project; agree the rules with the team; collect colleague feedback.
B) Agree the rules with the team; save them as project instructions; share the project; collect colleague feedback.
C) Collect colleague feedback; agree the rules with the team; share the project; save them as project instructions.
D) Share the project; collect colleague feedback; agree the rules with the team; save them as project instructions.
correct_answers: B) Agree the rules with the team; save them as project instructions; share the project; collect colleague feedback.
explanations: Writing the rules before the team has agreed them means the shared setup encodes one person's view.
Correct. Agree, encode, distribute, then learn from real use by the people who now depend on it.
Feedback is gathered before anything exists, and the instructions are saved only after sharing.
Colleagues are asked to review a project that has no agreed direction in it yet.
